name: Wynns Coonawarra Estate Cabernet Sauvignon John Riddoch 2012
text:
## Wynns Coonawarra Estate Cabernet Sauvignon John Riddoch 2012

**The story.** Wynns Coonawarra Estate is the historic heart of [Coonawarra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coonawarra_wine_region), a small wine region in the [Limestone Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limestone_Coast) of [South Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Australia), about 380 km south-east of [Adelaide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adelaide) and close to the Victorian border ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coonawarra_wine_region)). Its founder was the Scottish pioneer [John Riddoch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Riddoch) (1827–1901), "the Squire of Penola", a pastoralist and politician who moved to the district in 1861. In 1890 he divided 800 hectares of his red-soil land into the Coonawarra Fruit Colony, offering four-hectare blocks to settlers; 26 colonists began planting in 1891, putting in 95,000 vines and 10,000 fruit trees in the first year. In 1891 he built the famous triple-gabled winery, named Chateau Comaum ([Wynns heritage](https://www.wynns.com.au/en-au/discover/discover-our-heritage/)); the Coonawarra growers' association dates its completion to 1896 ([Coonawarra Vignerons](https://coonawarra.org/wineries/wynns-coonawarra-estate/)). The colony struggled, far from markets and in hard economic times, and Riddoch died at his home, Yallum Park, in 1901.

For half a century, Coonawarra was at a low ebb: most Australians drank fortified wine, and the old winery was destined to become a wool shed. Then in 1951 the Melbourne wine merchants Samuel Wynn and his son David bought it, with no expectation of profit ([Wynns heritage](https://www.wynns.com.au/en-au/discover/discover-our-heritage/); some accounts say 1953). David was the first Australian producer to use the word "estate" on a label to signal where a wine came from, and he commissioned the Melbourne artist Richard Beck to make a [woodcut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodcut) of the winery's three gables. That image has been on every Wynns Coonawarra Estate label since, one of Australia's most recognised wine symbols. Today Wynns is owned by [Treasury Wine Estates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treasury_Wine_Estates) and is the region's largest vineyard owner on terra rossa ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wynns_%28wine%29); [Coonawarra Vignerons](https://coonawarra.org/wineries/wynns-coonawarra-estate/)). Sue Hodder has been its senior winemaker since 1998, after her first vintage there in 1993.

**The land: terra rossa.** Coonawarra's fame rests on a strip of bright red soil, [terra rossa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terra_rossa_%28soil%29), just 15 km long and 2 km wide, north of [Penola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penola,_South_Australia). It lies on a shallow limestone ridge raised above the swampy land on either side, which is why the Riddoch Highway follows it; the soil is so red it shows clearly in aerial photos ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coonawarra_wine_region); [see it from above](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Wynns+Coonawarra+Estate,+Coonawarra,+South+Australia,+Australia&t=k)). Terra rossa, Italian for "red soil", gets its colour from iron ([hematite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hematite)) and drains surprisingly well for a clay soil, which vines love ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terra_rossa_%28soil%29)). Only 60 km from the sea, Coonawarra has a cool, maritime climate that Wikipedia compares to Bordeaux's, and it is "synonymous with Cabernet Sauvignon, full of plum and blackcurrant fruit" ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coonawarra_wine_region)).

**The wine: John Riddoch.** Named for the founder, John Riddoch Cabernet Sauvignon is Wynns' flagship, first made in 1982 and only released in years judged worthy of it. It takes typically less than 1% of Wynns' [Cabernet Sauvignon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabernet_Sauvignon) harvest, from two or three of its most distinguished mature vineyards on terra rossa. Sue Hodder describes the style as medium-bodied with moderate alcohol around 13%, meant to complement food rather than overwhelm it ([The Drinks Business](https://www.thedrinksbusiness.com/2025/12/wynns-john-riddoch-representing-the-ultimate-selection/)). In her words to Campbell Mattinson: "John Riddoch isn't meant to be a more concentrated version of Black Label. It's meant to be more complex" ([Halliday Wine Companion](https://winecompanion.com.au/articles/from-the-tasting-team/campbell-mattinson-on-wynns-jr-40-years)). The 2012 is 13.5% alcohol and sealed with a screwcap ([The Real Review](https://www.therealreview.com/wine-brands/4dnn8zb9szj2/)).

**The vintage.** [Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson)'s [South Australia vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/south-australia) says yields in 2012 were lower than average, blamed on high winds, drought and poor fruit set after the wet 2011. Quality, though, was much better than in the "exceptionally damp" 2011; South Australia avoided some of the weather extremes of other states, and the wines show strong varietal character.

**What the critics say for 2012.**
- **Campbell Mattinson, [Halliday Wine Companion](https://winecompanion.com.au/articles/from-the-tasting-team/campbell-mattinson-on-wynns-jr-40-years)** (40-year vertical tasting, October 2022). He scored every John Riddoch release from 2004 to 2019 at gold-medal level, 95 points or more, apart from the 2006, so the 2012 is among them. He found that after the 2000–2002 hiatus and a vineyard overhaul led by Hodder and viticulturist Allen Jenkins, the wine "has been on a stellar run", "about as reliably glorious as any Australian wine, bar none".
- **The Real Review**, the Australian and New Zealand review site, ranks the 2012 **#2 of 55** Coonawarra Cabernet Sauvignons from 2012 ([The Real Review](https://www.therealreview.com/wine-brands/4dnn8zb9szj2/)).
- **[James Suckling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Suckling)** (November 2017). His full note and score are behind a paywall; the visible part opens with "fabulous aromas of mint, spice, dark berry and chocolate" ([JamesSuckling.com](https://www.jamessuckling.com/tasting-notes/75013/wynns-cabernet-sauvignon-coonawarra-john-riddoch-2012)).
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 94.05** (from your CellarTracker list).
- Search results mention scores of 97 from Huon Hooke and 98 from Andrew Caillard MW for the 2012, but the merchant page they came from shows no reviews when I open it, so I can't confirm them and have left them out.

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is fourteen years old. Your CellarTracker list gives a long window, 2023 to 2042. Mattinson notes that history suggests these wines "go to another zone once they hit 20 years post vintage", so there's no hurry. Expect blackcurrant and plum with the region's signature mint, cedar and leafy notes, the tannins now softening. Decant an hour ahead.

**Serving.** Serve at about 16 to 18°C, a little below room temperature, in a large Bordeaux-style glass. A screwcap keeps the wine fresh, so there's no cork risk, but older bottles may have a little sediment.

**Food.** Hodder says the wine is made to go with food rather than overwhelm it. My picks: roast lamb with rosemary, a rare beef rib roast or [Beef Wellington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beef_Wellington), grilled [kangaroo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kangaroo_meat) fillet if you want to stay local, or an aged cheddar. I'd avoid very spicy dishes.

**Value and where to buy.** None of the three stores on this site lists the 2012. The Real Review shows it at about A$130 to NZ$150 ([The Real Review](https://www.therealreview.com/wine-brands/4dnn8zb9szj2/)), and back vintages turn up at auction. For a wine critics place among Australia's very best Cabernets, it is good value.

**From the history books**
- **The Squire of Penola.** [John Riddoch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Riddoch) (1827–1901), a Scottish-born pastoralist and South Australian politician, moved to the district in 1861 and founded the Coonawarra Fruit Colony in 1890 ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Riddoch); [Wynns heritage](https://www.wynns.com.au/en-au/discover/discover-our-heritage/)).
- **"Wild honeysuckle".** The name Coonawarra is said to come from the language of the Bindjali people, the Aboriginal Australians of the area, and to mean "wild honeysuckle" ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coonawarra_wine_region)).
- **From fortified to table wine.** Led by Wynns and [Penfolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penfolds), Coonawarra played a leading role in turning Australia from a country of [fortified wines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortified_wine) into a maker of world-class dry table wines ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coonawarra_wine_region)).
- **Michael, 1955.** In 1955 one 2,300-litre vat of Shiraz was so good it was bottled separately and named Michael, after David Wynn's first son; the idea was revived from 1990 ([Wynns heritage](https://www.wynns.com.au/en-au/discover/discover-our-heritage/)).
- **To Bordeaux.** John Riddoch became one of the first Australian wines sold through the Bordeaux merchants' system, La Place de Bordeaux; Wynns dates this to 2016, and The Drinks Business to the September 2021 campaign ([Wynns heritage](https://www.wynns.com.au/en-au/discover/discover-our-heritage/); [The Drinks Business](https://www.thedrinksbusiness.com/2025/12/wynns-john-riddoch-representing-the-ultimate-selection/)).

**Curious details**
- **The 12.1% that wasn't.** The label of the first, 1982, John Riddoch says 12.1% alcohol, often quoted as proof great wine doesn't need high alcohol. When Hodder had it analysed years later, it was actually 13% ([Halliday Wine Companion](https://winecompanion.com.au/articles/from-the-tasting-team/campbell-mattinson-on-wynns-jr-40-years)).
- **Made after a trip to Bordeaux.** The first John Riddoch was made by winemaker John Wade after a 1981 visit to [Bordeaux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bordeaux_wine), and it sold for $25 on release ([Halliday Wine Companion](https://winecompanion.com.au/articles/from-the-tasting-team/campbell-mattinson-on-wynns-jr-40-years)).
- **A boundary through a school vineyard.** Coonawarra's red soil sits beside black, poorly drained [rendzina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rendzina). The fight over where the region's border should run lasted eight years, and at least one vineyard, belonging to Penola High School, has the boundary running straight through it ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coonawarra_wine_region)).
- **Heritage-listed.** The historic Wynns winery on Memorial Drive is on the South Australian Heritage Register, and Coonawarra once had its own station on the [Mount Gambier railway line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Gambier_railway_line) ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coonawarra,_South_Australia)).
